name: ChurchBuilder
shortDescription: UK web-based church management software that can connect to an existing website or provide a combined website and administration system.
suitableContexts: Churches wanting one platform for a people database, groups, rotas and a website
Church groups needing shared administration with restricted access by church or group

pricing.summary: ChurchBuilder publishes Essential, Engage and Extend product tiers but the current public material reviewed here does not state their subscription prices. It states that recommended website templates typically have a one-off cost of around £50–£100.

tiers.label: Engage
tiers.detail: Adds calendars, rotas, activities and media

tiers.label: Extend
tiers.detail: Fuller church-management scope; training may be relevant

gdprInformation: Ask the supplier for current supplier data-processing terms, hosting location, sub-processors or retention arrangements. The church should obtain these before storing personal data.
integrations: Supplier states the management system can attach to an existing website or replace it

uk-purchasing.value: Supplier publishes a UK registered-business number and a Maidenhead registered address.

multi-site.value: Supplier describes an Extend configuration for groups of churches with restricted information access.

role-permissions.value: Supplier describes permissions and access restrictions in its people and multi-church material.

editorial.assessment: ChurchBuilder is a long-established UK option for churches that want their public website and administration system to work together, while retaining a route to attach the management tools to an existing site. The crucial decision is whether the church needs that combined model and has an owner for permissions, training and content, rather than simply replacing a directory.
bestFor: Churches combining a website with people, groups, rotas and resource booking
Multi-church groups needing shared administration with restricted access
Teams that prefer a staged Essential, Engage or Extend approach
strengths: Public material describes broad operational coverage across people, planning, communication and websites
Supports either an attached management system or a combined website
A UK registered business and UK support surface are visible
limitations: Ask the supplier about Current subscription prices, data-processing terms, hosting, exports, accessibility and migration support
A combined website and administration platform still needs named ownership for content, permissions and training
The church should validate web accessibility, data exit and security requirements in its own implementation

procurementVerdict.problem: Churches seeking linked website and administration tools
procurementVerdict.differentiator: Website, people, planning and resource booking are designed as one configurable product
procurementVerdict.firstCheck: Ask for current tier pricing and data terms, then trial actual permissions, rota and website-editor workflows
